summary_en: This work addresses the sparse-view limitation of acousto-optic tomography, where optical measurements provide line-integrated sound-pressure projections. A view-conditioned latent diffusion model synthesizes additional sound-field projections from measured views, and the generated projections are then used in volumetric reconstruction. Experiments show that augmenting nine observed views with nine synthesized views improves three-dimensional reconstruction accuracy, making this a direct computational acousto-optic image-formation paper.

summary_en: The paper replaces conventional piezoelectric or electromagnetic vector sensing with an acousto-optic vector hydrophone and derives a MUSIC-L orthogonal-subspace estimator for underwater acoustic wave-vector direction. Simulations and anechoic-tank experiments validate the system, with experimental errors below one degree under the reported setting. Although the output is directional sensing rather than a dense image, the optical acquisition of multidimensional acoustic information makes it a strong core addition to the repository's acousto-optic and underwater acoustic-sensing scope.

summary_en: This paper uses Fizeau interferometry to convert ultrasound-induced refractive-index changes in air into rapid, quantitative two-dimensional pressure-field maps. The method provides full-field optical acquisition without mechanical point scanning and is benchmarked against Schlieren visualization and an optical microphone. Because optical measurement is the primary mechanism for acoustic field imaging, this is a direct and high-confidence acoustic-optics repository addition.
